title: V1 evidence completeness and freeze, V1-S5-006-PR2
description: What V1-S5-006-PR2 verified before the V1 evidence pack could be frozen, and what it decided: every finding the V1-S5-006-PR1 normalization answered, and every finding this verification made, each with exactly one final state; how each executed record identifies the repository code that ran; the register changes this verification made, with the value before and after; the release blockers, each with the evidence that would close it; and the release gate those blockers decide.

finalStates.meaning: Committed evidence and citations now support the claim, or the finding was a record-keeping defect that has been corrected and verified.
The public statement or its limitation says only what the record supports, and the reduction is published where the claim is.
A claim status or an evidence level was lowered because the stronger proof is not present.
The historical record is kept exactly as written, and an additive correction beside it is authoritative for current use.
Required evidence is unavailable or contradictory, a certified claim depends on it, and the release gate stays incomplete until a named run or a decision closes it.

findingStates.verification: Re-read: the link claim holds a record of its own for the document-link suite, citing the V1-S5-002-PR2 record, which states 204 passed twice. The shell-check record stays for what it ran.

Re-read: the statement no longer says nine gates passed on the service, and a suite refuses that sentence in any current document. The limitation's corrected sentence about the infrastructure gates rests on a committed API read that itself says it certifies nothing, and the statement does not repeat it.
Re-read: the manifest-refusal record cites only the validator's own record, which supports the whole statement, and its chart version is the one that record names.

Re-read: the paved-road record under the claim installs a release, passes its release test, and removes it, so the install half the identifier names is cited. The claim is still a release blocker, for a different reason recorded under n04: the part of the statement only the scoped-cleanup record supports rests on code nothing identifies.

Re-read: the limitation says the statement, which says machine-checked, is what is certified, and names the two cleanup radii that were executed. The identifier is unchanged, because renaming it would break every surface that cites it.

Re-read: the statement says the workflow issued no mutating command between the delete and its closing uninstall, which the record establishes; no current document says no person intervened, and a suite keeps it that way.

Re-read: the statement names what was registered first and says the fixture was rewritten after the registered one was refused. The claim is still a release blocker, for a different reason recorded under n04: the code the baseline measured is identified by nothing.

Re-checked: the record is byte-for-byte what it was, by content hash, and the correction beside it names the pytest output as the count to read. The pinned run this change adds reports a later count for the same module at a named revision, and does not replace the historical one.

Re-read: the statement excepts the Linux branch of the processor-feature probe and says the diagnostics ran on one Windows host; the correction beside the record states the one exit 5 and why it was correct.

Re-checked: both names are values of the operator-set platform identifier and both records name the same model revision; the correction beside the closure record is unchanged and its record's content hash still matches.

Re-read: the record names a branch and no commit, and nothing else identifies the chart and Terraform code it ran; the chart version it names has carried ten chart states. The two later recovery runs, which do name their revisions, each say in their own records that they did not re-prove the artifact's survival. The claim stays a release blocker until the pod-restart workflow is repeated at a recorded revision.

Re-checked against the repository's history: the descriptor the register pins as executed, sha256 7220395254fe7da172d438df1252a59b66a376685937c94d5b7834276c4fdb59, is the LF-normalised content of deploy/serving/experiments/unready-model-recovery.v1.json at be0fa9adf623, the commit that first carried the run's files, and the run's environment file lists the same value among the files that decided the run.

Re-read: the claim holds a record whose per-query outcome is committed, and that record identifies the collector that ran by the version and build revision the collector reported about itself, 3.5.0 at 8be3a9560fbdd18a94dedec4b747c35178177202. No record observed the collector's image digest; both records say so, and no digest is borrowed from the chart.

Examined against committed code and configuration. The verification tool polls the collector's targets every 5 s until both jobs are up and then asks every query at once, and the two queries that read unexpectedly -- serving-runtime-scrape-job-absent and scrape-target-health-by-job -- read recording rules the chart evaluates every 30 s. A rule evaluation that ran before the runtime target's first scrape would record the absence as 1 and count only the API job, which accounts for both readings; the file keeps counts and no timestamps, so this is a mechanism consistent with the record and not a confirmed cause. Neither certified statement rests on either query: the collector claim's discovery and scraping rest on the targets API's own answer, both jobs up, and its evaluation clause on every asked query parsing. Both records keep the sample as a limitation.

Re-read: the replay record cites all three experiment records and the three capture files the replay tool reads, and its limitation says a held count is a count of 15-second steps over a 30-second scrape. The statement counts alerts and captures, not held steps, so the cadence bounds no published figure.

Re-read: where a distinct execution supported a part of a claim no cited record did, a record was added, including the three this change adds; no certified claim now rests on a coarse record for a fact its files do not report separately, and the index binds every cited file by its own hash.

Re-read: the closure run's provider stays unrecorded and no statement of the three claims that cite it names a provider. The model-hash and API-completion claims' limitations say that record names none; the quick start's statement is about a smoke run having been executed, not where.

Re-checked against the repository's history: the commit the baseline records name was created after the run's teardown, and the corrections beside both records are unchanged. What that means for the claim is recorded under n04.
Re-read: the manifest-refusal record's chart version, inferops-llm-0.2.0, is the value the only file it cites gives.
Re-checked: the record is unchanged by content hash and the correction beside it says the replay covers three captures.

Decided record by record. Of the 18 executed records that did not name the revision that ran, 13 no longer leave a claim's code unidentified: four pin the uncommitted part of their tree by content hashes that equal the files at a named commit, now cited; four involve no repository code among the claim-material components that executed and pin the third-party ones, one of them under a claim V1 does not make; three are under claims that gain a run of the same suites at a named revision; and two are under claims that hold another record which names its code and supports the statement. Five certified claims rest on code nothing identifies and are release blockers: the local baseline, the kind helper, the Helm uninstall's survival clause, the upgrade rollback, and the pod replacement.

findings.observation: The failure-and-resilience layer's note in docs/testing/test-strategy.v1alpha1.json said full C3 failure certification is out of V1 scope, pairing C3 with the superseded meaning in a current data file. The level-meaning guard reads Markdown and matches the capitalised pairing, so it saw neither.
findings.resolution: The note now says exhaustive failure testing is out of V1 scope and names no level. A test reads every current JSON data file under docs/ for the superseded pairings, in either case.

findings.observation: Four executed records name a base revision with the change's own files uncommitted. Each run wrote an environment file listing the LF-normalised SHA-256 of every file that decided it, and none of the four records cited that file, so the pins could not be used under the rule that a fact comes from a file the record cites.
findings.resolution: Each record now cites its run's environment file. Every one of the 34 hashes equals the LF-normalised content of its path at the commit that first carried the run's files, and a test checks each against the repository's history.

findings.observation: inferops-llm-0.3.0 is the chart version twelve records name, and the repository's history holds ten different trees of the chart that all carry that version. A chart version therefore does not identify the chart's content.
findings.resolution: No record is treated as identifying its chart by the version it names; the index page says a chart version is a label. Where a record also pins the chart's files by content, as the four content-pinned records do, that pin is what identifies it.

findings.observation: The API image the four content-pinned runs deployed is pinned by digest, localhost/inferops-api@sha256:9687e1bb11bd2b728bd61fd1338718a6816efa65958b9366cdf536fe8fdfc087, in the chart values those runs hashed. The same digest appears in three runs at three different base revisions, and no committed record says which source tree built it; it was published to no registry.
findings.resolution: The image is identified by an immutable digest, which is what the story asks of an image; the source revision that built it is not recorded, and the completeness report says so beside the four records. It is not a blocker, because the claims those runs support are about the release that digest names, and the digest is what ran.

findings.observation: The index page, the README's index row, and the testing and proof indexes described the freeze as an open decision for V1-S5-006-PR2, which is this change.
findings.resolution: They now state the decision: the evidence pack is not frozen, and why.

findings.observation: The scan of every cited file for prompts and responses found one: the Sprint 0 runtime feasibility record quotes the request it sent the runtime, a fixed project-authored question about Kubernetes, and the model's one-sentence reply. Every later record retains no prompt or completion text.
findings.resolution: Examined rather than removed. The prompt is a fixture the project wrote, it names no person, credential, host, or customer, and the reply is a general sentence about Kubernetes; neither is sensitive. The record is dated history and is left as written.

requiredEvidence.mustRecord: The commit printed and an empty status before and after, beside the artifact's byte count, SHA-256, inode, and modification time either side of the replacement; the workflow does not record the first two itself.

blockers.alternative: Decide the claim's status again with the maintainer. The recovery runs support that no acquisition Job appeared and the replacement served, which is a different and weaker statement than the artifact surviving.

releaseGate.reason: Five certified claims rest on evidence whose repository code nothing identifies. Each blocker names the run that would close it and the decision that could replace the run; until every one is closed, the evidence pack is not frozen and no later story may consume it as frozen.

contentPinReading: The commit that first carried each run's files has the run's base revision as its only parent, and under the compared code paths it changes only the files the run hashed and the package __init__ files named beside each pin, which re-export what the hashed modules define. So the chart, the Terraform, and the API source the run used are the base revision's, on the record's word that the hashed files are the ones that decided the run.
